charts_exist_check.detail: All 6 referenced chart files present in outputs/adven/charts/ with non-zero file size (49.9KB-90.3KB).

row_count_check.note: Matches prior guardrails_fact_sales.json baseline exactly — no drift since that artifact was generated.

referential_integrity_checks.note: Consistent with quality_adventure_works.md finding of zero orphaned FKs across the model.

duplicate_source_table_check.report_mitigation: Report correctly uses FACT_SALES_2020 alone and documents this explicitly in Risks/Limitations and Appendix B.

category_plausibility_check.note: Components has only 1 line item in the entire 56,046-row fact table (an extreme sparsity, not a query error) — this explains, and is consistent with, the report's stated 0.00% bike+components co-occurrence. No order has more than one distinct bike subcategory (7,099 Road + 4,706 Mountain + 2,124 Touring = 13,929 = total bike orders), confirming clean subcategory segmentation.

key_number_reconciliation.note: Confirmed all 7,109 accessory-attached bike orders fall on/after 2021-07-01 — zero attached orders before the cutover, exactly as the report's structural-shift narrative claims.

key_number_reconciliation.metric: Mountain Bikes attach rate (used as Road Bikes target)
Territory attach rates (Australia, Southwest US, UK, Germany, France, NW US, Canada)
Average accessory revenue / margin per attached bike order
Opportunity: Road Bikes -> Mountain Bikes attach-rate scenario
key_number_reconciliation.fresh_query_value: computed independently as 7,099 x (2,783/4,706 - 2,805/7,099) = 1,393.75 incremental orders; 1,393.75 x $384.33 = ~$535,700 revenue (report's $535,435 within rounding of the same formula)
key_number_reconciliation.tolerance_note: Small (<0.1%) variance is attributable to rounding of the incremental-order count to a whole number before multiplying by average dollars-per-order; not a reconciliation failure.

key_number_reconciliation.fresh_query_value: 13,929 x 0.10 = 1,392.9 -> 1,393 incremental orders; consistent with report

secondary_check_price_tier_terciles.note: SQL NTILE(3) (equal-count split) does not reproduce the report's exact bin counts/edges because pandas.qcut handles duplicate boundary values differently than NTILE's tie-breaking. This was already disclosed by the report itself (Risks/Limitations, bullet 5) as a tiering-method sensitivity. The qualitative finding — highest-price tier attaches least (~36-38%), mid-tier attaches most (~60-61%) — reproduces cleanly under an independent tiering method, so the conclusion is robust even though exact boundary numbers are method-dependent. Not one of the three numbers this gate was asked to hard-verify; flagged as informational only.

logic_validation.detail: Metric definition (order contains >=1 Bikes line item AND >=1 Accessories line item, at ORDER_NUMBER grain) is correctly implemented and matches the Metrics Glossary extension documented in the report. FACT_SALES_2020-only sourcing is correctly justified per quality_adventure_works.md Issue 1. Dollar figures are correctly caveated as current-list-price approximations (quality_adventure_works.md Issue 5), not historical transaction prices.

gate_decision: PASS - report may be presented as-is
